sites.name: Connecting Ridge C1
sites.note: Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters — the best-lit spot at the south pole (88% average illumination at 2 m).
sites.source: Gläser et al. 2018, Planet. Space Sci. (NASA NTRS 20170007365)

sites.name: Connecting Ridge C2
sites.note: Second ridge site of the same study (78.1% average illumination at 2 m).

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton
sites.note: Massif ~30 km from the pole; one of the original Artemis III candidate regions.
sites.source: Bussey et al. 2010, Icarus (Kaguya-based illumination study)

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim
sites.note: Rim of de Gerlache crater; Artemis III candidate region "de Gerlache Rim".

sites.name: Shackleton crater floor
sites.note: Cold trap that may hold water ice. Never sees the Sun or the Earth — shows why rovers must "commute" from lit ridges.
sites.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (crater center)

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.note: ~5 km high massif facing the Earth — long proposed for its line of sight to Earth.
sites.source: Artemis III candidate region (NASA, 2024); summit located in LOLA DEM

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.note: Highest mountain near the south pole; Artemis III candidate regions "Mons Mouton" and "Mons Mouton Plateau".
sites.source: IAU Gazetteer; summit located in LOLA DEM

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
sites.note: Rim of Nobile crater, one of the nine NASA Artemis III candidate regions (2024). Site DM2 ranked best for power, ISRU and human factors in a multi-criteria study.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (2024); site DM2 from arXiv:2406.19863 (Acta Astronautica, 2024)

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (CLPS)
sites.note: Intuitive Machines IM-2 intended landing site on Mons Mouton; landed 6 Mar 2025 (tipped over).
sites.source: LROC / NASA (Intuitive Machines IM-2 landing region)

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (CLPS)
sites.note: First CLPS landing (22 Feb 2024) near Malapert A crater, 300 km from the pole.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (ISRO)
sites.note: India's 2023 landing "Shiv Shakti point", the southernmost landing at the time.

sites.name: SLIM (JAXA)
sites.note: Japan's pinpoint lander (19 Jan 2024) near Shioli crater.

sites.name: Chang'e-4 (CNSA, far side)
sites.note: On the far side the Earth is always below the horizon — direct-to-Earth contact is impossible, so a relay satellite (Queqiao) is required.

sites.name: Apollo 11
sites.note: Equatorial site for contrast: the Sun climbs high and Earth hangs almost overhead.
